core.headline: End-of-terrace Victorian cottage in Smarden Conservation Area
core.listing:
2 Forge Cottages is an end-of-terrace Victorian cottage dating from around 1880, built of red brick under a clay-tiled roof. The property stands within the Smarden Conservation Area.

The sitting room measures 3.90m x 3.60m (12'10" x 11'10") and has a cast-iron fireplace. Ledged-and-braced doors feature throughout. The kitchen/dining room measures 4.30m x 3.20m (14'1" x 10'6") and has a quarry-tiled floor and a range alcove. The kitchen beams are reclaimed, installed in the 1990s.

On the first floor, bedroom 1 measures 3.80m x 3.30m (12'6" x 10'10") and bedroom 2 measures 2.90m x 2.40m (9'6" x 7'10"). There is one bathroom.

The rear cottage garden extends approx. 12m (40ft) and has a brick path and a timber shed.

The village pub is approx. 2 minutes' walk. Parking is on-street.

Guide Price £425,000. Freehold. Council Tax Band C (Ashford Borough Council). EPC rating E. Construction: standard – red brick under a clay-tiled roof. Mains electricity and mains water (not metered). Sewerage: septic tank. Oil-fired central heating. Broadband: FTTC. Mobile signal: good outdoors, variable indoors. The property is within the Smarden Conservation Area. The septic tank is shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; there are access rights for maintenance and emptying costs are shared. The rear of the garden is in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded. Restricted head height at top of stairs, approx. 1.88m (6'2"). The seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules.
core.summary: Guide Price £425,000. End-of-terrace Victorian cottage dating from around 1880 in the Smarden Conservation Area, with cast-iron fireplace, quarry-tiled kitchen floor, cottage garden and village pub approx. 2 minutes' walk.
